people as possible, both young and old, excursions which
enable them to come into direct contact with nature, to
enjoy the beauty of nature and from their enjoyment to gain
renewed energy and power for their work.
This, to be sure, is how a wise administration calculates
and we can be thankful for this development. But as
Christians we must say still more. As Christians we believe
that we have not deeply enough understood the meaning of
our joy in nature which discloses its beauty to us in the spring
if we regard this joy in biological terms, as it were, as some-
thing to be cultivated for the sake of the health of our nation.
As Christians we must go still further. In what way? What
is the real gift of nature which the generous hand of spring
lavishes upon us as a shower of blossoms? What is the real
meaning of the joy which awakens within us and fills our
being? There can be no doubt as to the answer. The real
gift of nature is that it speaks to us of God the Creator; and
the real meaning of our joy is that here we feel ourselves
coming into communion with the very ground of our being
and perceiving its sustaining energies. Thus our joy passes
into thankfulness and adoration, adoration of the presence of
God in nature.
"While the earth remains..." It is the law of God which
prevails in the rhythm of nature's life. And when we grow
aware of the triumphant power and luxuriant abundance of
nature, we are asked whether we realize that the law which
governs its processes is the law of God.
This is a dangerous way of speaking! We know very well
those misleading voices which in our time declare: it is in
nature, in its infallible courses and eternal energies, that God
reveals Himself to us. We should turn our attention to this
revelation, not to an outmoded book which raises the un-
justified claim of being God's self-revelation. We cannot
doubt as Christians that we must not follow such teaching,
that God has revealed Himself to man in His Word and does
